claims.claim: Sun Yat-sen proposed a large dam across the Yangtze in his 1919 work The International Development of China.
claims.episode_span: dates to Sun Yat-sen’s 1919 proposal to improve navigation and irrigation on the Yangtze
claims.supporting_quote: Sun Yat-sen envisioned a large dam across the Yangtze River in The International Development of China (1919).

claims.claim: The 1954 Yangtze flood killed more than 30,000 people (33,167) and displaced millions.
claims.episode_span: devastating floods in 1954 that killed more than 30,000 people and displaced millions
claims.supporting_quote: The river flooded in 1954 over an area of 193,000 km 2 (74,500 mi 2 ) , killing 33,167 people and forcing almost 18.9 million people to move.

claims.claim: The National People's Congress approved the dam in 1992, with an unusually large share of delegates opposing or abstaining.
claims.episode_span: The National People’s Congress formally approved construction in 1992
claims.supporting_quote: The National People's Congress approved the dam in 1992: of 2,633 delegates, 1,767 voted in favour, 177 voted against, 664 abstained, and 25 members did not vote,

claims.claim: Construction started on December 14, 1994, at Sandouping in Hubei Province.
claims.episode_span: Construction began in 1994 at Sandouping in Hubei Province.
claims.supporting_quote: is a hydroelectric gravity dam that spans the Yangtze River near Sandouping in Yiling District , Yichang , Hubei province, central China, downstream of the Three Gorges .

claims.claim: The dam's installed generating capacity is 22,500 MW, and it was expected to supply about 10% of China's power.
claims.episode_span: flood-storage capacity of 22 billion cubic meters and a generating capacity of 22,500 megawatts
claims.supporting_quote: The Three Gorges Dam is the world's largest capacity hydroelectric power station, with 34 generators: 32 main generators, each with a capacity of 700 MW, and two plant power generators, each with capacity of 50 MW, for a total of 22,500 MW.

claims.claim: The reservoir's flood storage capacity is about 22 cubic kilometres (22 billion cubic meters).
claims.episode_span: flood-storage capacity of 22 billion cubic meters
claims.supporting_quote: The reservoir's flood storage capacity is 22 km 3 (5.3 mi 3 ; 18 million acre⋅ft ) . This capacity will reduce the frequency of major downstream flooding from once every 10 years to once every 100 years.

claims.claim: At maximum level 175 m, the reservoir averages about 660 km in length and holds 39.3 cubic kilometres (about 39 billion tonnes) of water; the 175 m level was reached by 2010.
claims.episode_span: the added weight of approximately 39 billion tons of water altered stresses on the crust beneath the 660-kilometer reservoir
claims.supporting_quote: When the water level is at its maximum of 175 m (574 ft) above sea level, 110 m (361 ft) higher than the river level downstream, the dam reservoir is on average about 660 km (410 mi) in length and 1.12 km (3,675 ft) in width. It contains 39.3 km 3 (31,900,000 acre⋅ft ) of water

claims.claim: Estimates of the number of people displaced by the dam's construction range from 1.13 million to around 1.4 million, consistent with the episode's 1.13 million figure; planning estimated 13 cities and over a thousand villages affected.
claims.episode_span: the relocation of roughly 1.13 million residents from 13 cities and hundreds of villages
claims.supporting_quote: Estimates of the number of people displaced by the dam's construction range from 1.13 million to around 1.4 million.

claims.claim: The Qianjiangping landslide of July 2003, triggered as the initial impoundment reached 135 m, killed 24 people in Zigui County.
claims.episode_span: the 2003 Qianjiangping slide killed 24 people and blocked a tributary
claims.source_title: Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution - landslide monitoring in the Three Gorges Reservoir Area
claims.supporting_quote: One notable event was the Qianjiangping landslide, occurring on July 14, 2003, in Zigui County, Hubei Province, induing by the initial impoundment reaching 135 m above sea level. This event led to the unfortunate loss of 24 lives, the destruction of 129 residential structures,

claims.claim: Studies found earthquake frequency in the reservoir area is correlated with water levels and increased markedly after impoundment, though limited to micro and small events.
claims.episode_span: Seismic stations recorded a measurable increase in small earthquakes
claims.supporting_quote: earthquake frequency is significantly correlated to water levels [ 100 ] , and has "remarkably increased compared to that before water impoundment"

claims.claim: The dam traps much of the Yangtze's sediment load, reducing sediment delivery downstream.
claims.episode_span: the dam trapped most of the Yangtze’s sediment load, starving the river channel and coastal delta
claims.supporting_quote: Because the flow is slower above the dam, much of this sediment settles there instead of flowing downstream, and there is less sediment downstream.

claims.claim: Premier Li Peng, a hydraulic engineer by background, championed the Three Gorges Dam and initiated its construction.
claims.episode_span: Premier Li Peng, a hydraulic engineer by training, championed the project
claims.supporting_quote: He spent much of his time monitoring what he considered his life's work to have been, the Three Gorges Dam . Li's interest in the Dam reflected his earlier career as a hydraulic engineer,

claims.claim: The dam generates on the order of 100 TWh of electricity per year (95±20 TWh on average; 101.6 TWh in 2018).
claims.episode_span: the structure still supplies roughly 100 terawatt-hours annually
claims.supporting_quote: it generates 95±20 TWh of electricity per year on average, depending on the amount of precipitation in the river basin.
